covered.concept: Python for ML ecosystem (NumPy, pandas, matplotlib, scikit-learn API)
covered.why: Learner knows Python but not ML stack; hands-on fluency with arrays, DataFrames, and sklearn API is prerequisite for every subsequent step.

covered.concept: Supervised learning framing (classification vs regression)
covered.why: Core mental model — determines task type, loss function, metric, and model family; conceptual clarity prevents category errors later.

covered.concept: Train/validation/test split & cross-validation
covered.why: Non-negotiable for credible evaluation; must implement stratified splits and k-fold CV to avoid leakage and variance underestimation.

covered.concept: Model evaluation metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC, RMSE, MAE)
covered.why: Metric choice encodes business objective; must compute, interpret, and justify each for classification and regression.

covered.concept: Feature preprocessing (scaling, encoding, missing values, datetime, text)
covered.why: Real data is messy; ColumnTransformer pipelines prevent train/serve skew — the #1 production failure mode.

covered.concept: Linear models (logistic/linear regression with regularization)
covered.why: Interpretable baseline; regularization (L1/L2) teaches bias-variance tradeoff concretely; fast to train and debug.

covered.concept: Tree-based models (decision trees, random forests, gradient boosting)
covered.why: Industry standard for tabular data; random forest gives strong baseline with minimal tuning; gradient boosting is SOTA.

covered.concept: Gradient boosting libraries (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost)
covered.why: CatBoost handles categoricals natively — highest leverage for weekend learner; must tune n_estimators, learning_rate, depth.

covered.concept: Hyperparameter tuning (grid search, random search, Bayesian optimization)
covered.why: Random search + CV is learnable in hours and dramatically improves results; Bayesian is mention-only (Optuna demo).

covered.concept: Model selection & comparison
covered.why: Practical skill: compare 2-3 model families quickly, know what to try and when to stop; uses CV scores + training time.

covered.concept: Overfitting/underfitting diagnosis & regularization
covered.why: Core diagnostic skill — learning curves, validation gaps, regularization paths; prevents silent production failures.

covered.concept: Imbalanced data handling (resampling, class weights, threshold tuning)
covered.why: Real production data is imbalanced; threshold tuning is high-ROI, zero-retrain technique; class_weight='balanced' is default.

covered.concept: Pipeline construction (sklearn Pipeline, ColumnTransformer)
covered.why: Single most important production pattern — encapsulates preprocessing + model, prevents skew, enables serialization/serving.

covered.concept: Experiment tracking (MLflow, Weights & Biases, ClearML)
covered.why: Lightweight local MLflow teaches reproducibility in 30 min; log params, metrics, artifacts — mental model for team scale.

covered.concept: Model serialization & versioning (joblib, ONNX, model registry)
covered.why: joblib for sklearn, ONNX for portability; model registry concept (staging/production) is essential mental model.

covered.concept: Model serving patterns (REST API, batch inference, streaming, edge)
covered.why: Must understand deployment targets; REST + batch covers 90% of cases; streaming/edge mentioned for awareness.

covered.concept: API frameworks for ML (FastAPI, Flask, Triton, TorchServe)
covered.why: FastAPI is Pythonic, async, auto-docs — teaches serving pattern in one file; Pydantic validates input schema.

covered.concept: Containerization for ML (Docker, multi-stage builds, GPU images)
covered.why: Docker is universal deployment artifact; minimal multi-stage Dockerfile + .dockerignore teachable in 20 minutes.

covered.concept: Data validation & schema enforcement (Great Expectations, pandera, TFDV)
covered.why: pandera/sklearn validation in 15 min prevents silent data drift failures; schema as contract between training and serving.

covered.concept: Responsible ML (fairness, interpretability, SHAP, LIME, privacy)
covered.why: SHAP for tree models is fast to learn and essential for stakeholder trust; fairness/privacy mentioned as awareness.

modules.capability: Design, train, evaluate, and deploy a production-ready ML model end-to-end: frame a business problem as supervised learning, build a preprocessing+model pipeline with ColumnTransformer, compare linear/tree/boosting baselines with cross-validation, diagnose overfitting and handle imbalance, serialize the pipeline to joblib/ONNX, wrap it in a FastAPI service with Pydantic validation, containerize it with a multi-stage Dockerfile, and log experiments in MLflow — all on a real tabular dataset.
modules.why_here: Single weekend capacity with zero ML background demands one contiguous learning arc — every concept builds toward the same deployed model artifact; the learner must internalize the full preprocessing → training → evaluation → packaging → serving chain in 48 hours, and no subset delivers the target capability alone.
